textos: A cathedral with a 45-metre hole in its roof.
For decades, nobody knew how to close it.
Domes needed a timber frame. This one was too big.
A goldsmith, Filippo Brunelleschi, says he can. He won’t say how.
Two domes in one: one carries the weight, one keeps out the rain.
Pointed, not round: a radius four-fifths of the span.
Herringbone bricks: each ring holds itself up as it rises.
Chains of stone and wood bind it like the hoops of a barrel.
Sixteen years. Four million bricks. 37,000 tonnes.
Six centuries on, it is still the largest brick dome ever built.
